summary: The petition challenged the constitutional validity of 27% reservation for OBC (non-creamy layer) and 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in All-India Quota (AIQ) seats for medical admissions (UG and PG) under NEET. The Court upheld the validity of OBC reservation in AIQ seats, affirming the Executive's power to implement such reservations based on constitutional provisions and prior jurisprudence. It held that AIQ seats, though initially domicile-free, are amenable to reservation under Article 15(5). The Court reasoned that equity demands inclusion of socially and educationally backward classes even in centralized quotas, and that introducing OBC reservation prospectively from 2021-22 did not constitute unfair alteration of rules mid-stream. The EWS reservation was referred for separate adjudication. The judgment emphasized non-discrimination and equal opportunity while affirming affirmative action.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 15(5) of the Constitution of India
Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admissions) Act, 2006
Dr Pradeep Jain v. Union of India
Dinesh Kumar (I) v. Motilal Nehru Medical College
Abhay Nath v. University of Delhi
final_judgment: The petition challenging the OBC reservation in AIQ seats was dismissed, and the constitutional validity of 27% OBC reservation in 15% UG and 50% PG AIQ seats was upheld; the issue of EWS reservation was referred for final hearing in March 2022.
